name: Bin el Ouidane Lake
hero_subtitle: Turquoise alpine reservoir framed by red cliffs — boating and lakeside relaxation.

overview.title: A turquoise lake in the Atlas foothills
overview.p1: Bin el Ouidane is a large reservoir with striking turquoise water set against red and ochre hills. It is a favourite stop for views, boat trips and lakeside meals.
overview.p2: Hotels and restaurants line parts of the shore. The drive from Azilal or Beni Mellal is scenic and well paved.
overview.p3: Ideal to combine with Ouzoud or a return toward Marrakech. Sunset light on the water is especially beautiful.

food.title: Where to eat at Bin el Ouidane
food.p1: Hotels and restaurants along the shore serve grills, lake fish and standard Moroccan dishes with views of the reservoir.
food.li1: Grilled meats and fish on lakeside terraces
food.li2: Tagines and salads at hotel restaurants
food.li3: Mint tea with a view of the water
food.li4: Reserve a table at peak weekends
food.li5: Combine with a boat trip if available
food.p2: Cash remains useful for small local places.

tips.title: Practical tips — Bin el Ouidane Lake

1.title: Access
1.desc: Well-paved road from Azilal or Beni Mellal. Parking near hotels and viewpoints.

2.title: Activities
2.desc: Boat rides are popular when available; check locally for schedules.

3.title: Stay
3.desc: Overnight at a lakeside hotel for sunset and a quieter morning.

q1.question: How much time for Bin el Ouidane Lake?
q1.answer: Plan at least the duration indicated in the info box; longer stays reward hikers.

q2.question: Is it suitable for children?
q2.answer: Yes with supervision on paths and near water or cliffs.

q3.question: Do I need a guide?
q3.answer: Not always required, but recommended for valleys and remote tracks.

q4.question: How to get there?
q4.answer: By road from Azilal, Marrakech or Beni Mellal; 4x4 helpful on some mountain roads.
